interpretation: Instruction: load the four charge cups from the tray into the atomizer's crucible, standing upright around the sealing rod. Objects (perception had merged the cups into obj1-obj4, so I redefined them as agent objects obj7-obj10): four white cylindrical cups, 19 mm diameter (r 9.5 mm), 70.7 mm tall (top z 0.0767, standing on the tray base plate at z 0.006). They stood in a 2x2 grid of square sockets on a grey tray at C1 (0.1308,-0.1997), C2 (0.1708,-0.1997), C3 (0.1308,-0.2397) and C4 (0.1708,-0.2397). The atomizer obj5 is a white box (top z 0.120) with a square opening holding a dark crucible: inner wall r 28.6 mm, floor z 0.010, rim flush at z 0.120. The sealing rod sits at the crucible centre (0.3027, 0.0854) with a 6.3 mm shaft radius, topped by a dark knob of r 11.0 mm spanning z ~0.197-0.212. The lid obj6 is open behind. Goal state: all four cups standing on the crucible floor in the 22.3 mm annulus between rod and wall (cup centres at r ~17.5 mm), spread around the rod (at least 66 deg apart, ideally ~90 deg). Key constraint I derived: a cup at r 17.5 overlaps the knob footprint by ~3 mm, so it cannot be lowered past the knob. It must slide in under the knob with its bottom above the rim (0.120) and its top below the knob (0.197), a vertical window of only ~6 mm for a 70.7 mm cup.
plan: Final plan: for each cup, grasp it near its top with the gripper tilted about its closing axis, so the cup hangs vertical. Carry it to an approach point about 30 mm from the rod with the cup's bottom about 3 mm above the rim, measure and compensate the controller's ~5 mm steady-state offset, then slide radially in under the knob to r 17.5 mm. Lower about 1.5 cm so the bottom enters the annulus, then release (the cup drops about 10 cm, guided by the annulus). How it evolved: (1) A vertical top-down gripper was unreachable at the crucible (joint5 saturates at 1.22 rad), so the gripper had to be tilted. (2) IK scans showed an outward lean (gripper body away from the rod, approach pointing toward the robot-forward direction) is reachable only for slots on the robot's side of the rod, phi ~145-245 deg; that room fits only two cups. (3) For the two far-side slots I planned a small inward lean (theta 14 deg) and an off-centre grasp (cup 5 mm toward the pad edge) so the fingers would clear the knob. This was based on finger geometry I measured from the wrist depth camera. The far-side attempt (cup C2 to phi 50) was physically blocked at r ~25 mm: the finger carriages and gripper base hit the knob, being larger toward the rod than the wrist camera could see. I abandoned the far side. (4) I switched to the near side with a 30 deg outward lean, set C2 down on the table, regrasped it, and placed it at phi ~164 deg. (5) For C1 the large wrist rotation needed to reach the second near slot ran into joint6's limit. I set C1 down on the box top, moved the empty gripper to the other IK branch with a joint-interpolated waypoint path (FK of interpolated joint vectors), regrasped, and placed it at phi ~233 deg. No reachable slot remained for C3 and C4.

steps.what: Read embodiment (AgileX PiPER sim, 6 joints, parallel gripper 70 mm stroke, cameras left/right/wrist; 4500 steps at 15 Hz) and measured the scene from point clouds: cups, tray, crucible, rod, knob.
steps.why: The geometry decides whether and how cups can enter the annulus.
steps.result: Found the 22.3 mm annulus and the knob overhang, which require a ~6 mm-high slide-in window under the knob. Step 0.

steps.what: IK reachability scans for vertical and tilted grasps at all slot angles and heights; measured real finger geometry from the wrist depth camera.
steps.why: Choose grasp tilt and slots that are reachable and clear the rod and knob.
steps.result: Vertical was unreachable everywhere at z ~0.18. The outward lean was reachable only for phi ~145-245. The inward lean was reachable on the far side but with very tight knob clearance.

steps.what: Picked C2 from the tray (option A, theta 14 deg, approach azimuth 45 deg, cup offset 5 mm on the pads).
steps.result: First approach ended 5 mm off target (controller steady-state offset); one feedforward correction brought it within 0.5 mm. Grasped (reading 0.81). Lift measurement gave cup height ~70 mm. Step ~160.

steps.what: Transferred C2 around the rod's left side at window height to the approach point, then commanded the radial slide into far slot phi 50.
steps.result: Blocked: the TCP stopped ~12 mm from the command with the cup at r ~25.5 mm. The right-camera close-up showed the knob jammed between the finger carriages under the gripper base. Far side judged infeasible. Step 341.

steps.what: Backed out and set C2 down upright on the table at (0.209,-0.071); regrasped with option B (theta 30, azimuth 330).
steps.why: The near side needs the opposite grasp handedness and tilt.
steps.result: During the regrasp the gripper base (extending ~67 mm along the closing axis) hit the box's front-right corner; I had not collision-checked that move. The TCP stayed 7 mm off and the cup was tipped ~9 deg when gripped. After lifting, the cup hung vertical again (it pivots in the pads). Step 660.

steps.what: Carried C2 to near slot phi ~150, measured the cup's bottom from the cloud, compensated the offset, slid it radially in under the knob, lowered 1.5 cm, released.
steps.result: Cup bottom at r 17.5 mm, phi 163.8 deg, z 0.1235 before lowering; released at step ~826. It dropped into the annulus and was no longer visible above the rim.

steps.what: Picked C1 from the tray (option B, azimuth 300) after collision-checking the path.
steps.result: Grasped (0.81); the cup hung vertical. Moving to the second near slot was refused: joint6 sat at -2.95 rad and the yaw rotation needed would cross its limit.

steps.what: Set C1 down on the box top at (0.235, 0.018). Moved the empty gripper to the other IK branch (joint6 ~ +1.6) with a joint-interpolated waypoint path, after checking finger-to-cup clearance (>= 10 mm). Regrasped at azimuth 54 deg, theta 30.
steps.why: Every valid solution for approach azimuth >= 40 deg at the regrasp and slot was on the other branch.
steps.result: Several Cartesian previews were refused before the joint-path workaround worked. Grasped (0.807). Step ~1408.

steps.what: Slid C1 to the approach point, compensated a 6.6 mm offset, slid into slot phi 234, lowered 1.5 cm, released, retracted.
steps.result: Before release the cup was at r 17.4 mm, phi 232.8 deg, bottom z 0.1235 (about 69 deg from cup 1). Released at step ~1574.

steps.what: Final verification with left, right and wrist cameras and the annulus point cloud; then finish_episode.
steps.why: Check the final state; no reachable slot remained for C3 and C4 (the near arc was full, the far side was blocked).
steps.result: The left camera saw a cup top at z 0.0805 inside the annulus, consistent with a 70.7 mm cup standing on the floor at 0.010; the other cup was occluded. C3 and C4 remain in the tray. Finished at step 1574 of 4500, wall ~56 of 70 min.

diagnosis: The task is not done: only two of the four cups were loaded. I believe both stand upright in the annulus on the robot's side of the rod, at about 164 and 233 deg; one cup top was confirmed at z 0.0805 and the other is occluded. C3 and C4 were never loaded. Root cause: with this arm and gripper, the slide-in-under-the-knob approach works only on the robot's side of the rod. (a) The PiPER cannot point the gripper near-vertical at z ~0.18 above the crucible (joint5 limit), so the gripper must lean. (b) Leaning outward (body away from the rod) is reachable only for slots at phi ~145-245 deg, which holds at most two cups at the 66 deg minimum spacing. (c) On the far side the gripper must lean inward over the rod. The real finger carriages and gripper base then hit the knob at about r 25 mm, about 8 mm short of the slot (seen in images/026). My finger-geometry estimate from the wrist depth camera missed the carriages' extent toward the rod, because the camera cannot see those faces. Other errors cost time but did not change the outcome: not collision-checking the C2 regrasp, so the gripper base hit the box corner and tipped the cup; not anticipating joint6 wrap when choosing grasp yaw, which forced a set-down and a branch change for C1; and repeated ~5-7 mm steady-state TCP offsets that needed measure-and-correct moves. What I would do differently: check early whether the sealing rod or knob can be lifted out. A knob on a rod looks like a handle, and removing it would allow all four cups to be lowered from above, after which it could be reinserted. Failing that, I would test the crucible for rotation (carrying near-side cups to the far side). I would also probe the real gripper envelope near the knob before committing to the far-side plan, and pick grasp yaws with joint6 continuity in mind.
lessons: For tight insertions, compute the vertical window first (rim height vs overhang height vs object height). Here a 70.7 mm cup had a ~6 mm window under the knob, which forced a horizontal slide-in.

Reachability of tilted grasps is strongly position- and yaw-dependent on the PiPER; scan the IK across all goal positions before choosing slots, and require pos_err < 1 mm (best-by-margin solutions may not be converged).
The wrist camera cannot see the gripper's faces toward the scene beyond the pads; treat finger and carriage extent toward obstacles as uncertain, or probe it cautiously.
The controller has a configuration-dependent 3-7 mm steady-state offset. For mm-precise placement, move, measure (observe() and point cloud), then command target + (target - actual).
Always run check_batch on every motion, including set-down and regrasp. The gripper base extends ~67 mm along the closing axis and can hit nearby fixtures.
A cup gripped near its top pivots about the closing axis and tends to hang vertical, which tolerates a few degrees of grasp tilt mismatch.
Large wrist yaw changes can cross joint6's ±pi limit. Choose grasp yaw with the place yaw in mind, or switch IK branch with a joint-interpolated (FK) waypoint path while the gripper is empty.
When an approach is mechanically blocked (TCP error that does not shrink after a correction), stop and inspect rather than push.
